# About this qmd

This qmd includes the national analysis: all 2,462 PUMAs in the 50
states and DC.

It reads two saved files and joins them:

-   `data/final/national_puma_dataset_2022_2024.gpkg` from
    `processing_national_pumas_2022_2024.qmd`: outcomes, controls and
    PUMA boundaries
-   `data/final/puma_prison_exposure.csv` from
    `processing_prison_exposure.qmd`: the prison exposure measures

Outcomes:

-   `overdose_rate_2022_2024`: overdose deaths per 100,000, pooled
    2022–2024 (CDC tract data)
-   `pct_divorced_past_yr`: % of ever-married people who divorced in the
    past year, pooled 2022–2024 ACS

Exposure: distance-decay exposure to open state and federal prisons, Σ
exp(−d/h) over all prisons, built for each tract and averaged over the
PUMA's tracts with non-institutional population as weights. The main
measure is h = 10 km (?); h = 1, 5 and 25 km, the number of prisons
inside the PUMA and any prison inside the PUMA are reported alongside
it.

# Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(gt)
library(broom)
library(fixest)
library(spdep)
library(spatialreg)
library(tigris)
library(patchwork)
library(marginaleffects)
library(mgcv)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
set.seed(2024)
```

## Data

```{r}
#| label: data-load
# Exposure measures from processing_prison_exposure.qmd, outcomes and controls (with boundaries) from processing_national_pumas_2022_2024.qmd
exposure <- read_csv("data/final/puma_prison_exposure.csv",
                     col_types = cols(GEOID20 = col_character()))

puma_geo <- st_read("data/final/national_puma_dataset_2022_2024.gpkg", quiet = TRUE) %>%
  select(-any_of(setdiff(names(exposure), "GEOID20"))) %>%   
  left_join(exposure, by = "GEOID20")

puma_df <- puma_geo %>% st_drop_geometry()

nrow(puma_df)   # 2462

# Outcomes and their labels
outcomes <- c(
  overdose_rate_2022_2024 = "Overdose deaths per 100,000",
  pct_divorced_past_yr    = "% of ever-married divorced in past year"
)

# Lower 48 for maps (Alaska and Hawaii are not included)
puma_geo_l48 <- puma_geo %>%
  filter(!state_fips %in% c("02", "15")) %>%
  st_transform(5070)

# Open state and federal prisons
prisons <- st_read("data/raw/prison-boundaries-1-geojson.geojson", quiet = TRUE) %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%
  filter(STATUS == "OPEN", TYPE %in% c("STATE", "FEDERAL")) %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  st_transform(5070) %>%
  st_filter(st_union(puma_geo_l48))
```

# DESCRIPTIVES

## Summary statistics

```{r}
#| label: summary-stats
summary_vars <- c(names(outcomes),
                  "prison_exp_h1", "prison_exp_h5", "prison_exp_h10", "prison_exp_h25",
                   "num_prisons_in_puma",
                  "pop_density", "pct_pop_rural", "pct_pop_nonmetro")

puma_df %>%
  select(all_of(summary_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable") %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(!is.na(value)),
            mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE), median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = summary_vars)) %>%
  arrange(variable) %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(mean, sd, min, median, max), decimals = 2) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Summary statistics, PUMAs (2022–2024)")

table(puma_df$prison_present_in_puma, useNA = "ifany")  #PUMAs with/without a prison inside
```

## Maps

```{r}
#| label: map-setup

# Census region outlines: state boundaries dissolved by region
region_map <- tigris::states(cb = TRUE, year = 2020, progress_bar = FALSE) %>%
  filter(STATEFP %in% unique(puma_geo_l48$state_fips)) %>%
  left_join(
    tibble(STUSPS = c(state.abb, "DC"),
           region = c(as.character(state.region), "South")) %>%
      mutate(region = recode(region, "North Central" = "Midwest")),
    by = "STUSPS"
  ) %>%
  st_transform(st_crs(puma_geo_l48)) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise()

# Pieces shared by the maps
map_theme    <- list(theme_void(), theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")))
region_layer <- geom_sf(data = region_map, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4)
prison_layer <- geom_sf(data = prisons, size = 0.5, colour = "deepskyblue3", alpha = 0.7)
```

### Outcomes

```{r}
#| label: map-overdose
ggplot(puma_geo_l48) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = overdose_rate_2022_2024), colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Per 100,000", option = "magma", direction = -1,
                       na.value = "grey85") +
  region_layer +
  labs(title = "Overdose death rate, 2022–2024") +
  map_theme
```

```{r}
#| label: map-overdose-years
# one map per year
puma_geo_l48 %>%
  select(GEOID20, overdose_rate_2022, overdose_rate_2023, overdose_rate_2024) %>%
  pivot_longer(starts_with("overdose_rate_"), names_to = "year", values_to = "rate",
               names_prefix = "overdose_rate_") %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = rate), colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Per 100,000", option = "magma", direction = -1,
                       na.value = "grey85") +
  region_layer +
  facet_wrap(~ year, ncol = 1) +
  labs(title = "Overdose death rate by year") +
  map_theme
```

When we look at the overdose rates for each year separately, we see that
2024 has much lower rates across the whole country (a drop of about
24%). A quick google search confirms this and attributes it to new state
policies and access to nalaxone (narcan). This makes me wonder whether
pooling all these years into one dataset is still okay, and whether I
should find a way to also control for access to nalaxone or for
drug/healthcare policies at the state level(or state fixed effects are
enough)?

```{r}
#| label: map-divorce
ggplot(puma_geo_l48) +

                       na.value = "grey85") +

```

```{r}
#| label: map-divorce-years
#| fig-height: 9
# One map per year, same colour scale so the years can be compared
puma_geo_l48 %>%

  pivot_longer(starts_with("pct_divorced_past_yr_20"), names_to = "year", values_to = "rate",
```

The divorce rates seem more stable across the years.

### Prisons and exposure

```{r}
#| label: map-prisons
# where the prisons are (open state and federal facilities)
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = puma_geo_l48, fill = "grey95", colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.05) +
  region_layer +
  geom_sf(data = prisons, aes(colour = TYPE), size = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(STATE = "firebrick", FEDERAL = "navy"), name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Open state and federal prisons") +
  map_theme
```

Exposure at the four decay scales (h=1, h=5, h=10, h=25)

I am still conflicted about which of these four should be “the main
measure”... I know for sure that it is not going to be 25 km, because
that is too far and does not really make sense. Conceptually, h = 1 and
h = 5 make the most sense to me, but because few such places exist, I am
wondering whether it makes sense to use them. Also, when running the
models, we can see that the effect and its significance fade/weaken as h
increases, so maybe I actually need all of them...?

```{r}
exp_h10 <- ggplot(puma_geo_l48) +
```

Count-based exposure measures:

```{r}
#| label: map-prison-presence
# PUMAs with at least one open state or federal prison inside their boundary
puma_geo_l48 %>%
  mutate(presence = if_else(prison_present_in_puma == 1, "Prison in PUMA", "No prison")) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = presence), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Prison in PUMA" = "firebrick", "No prison" = "grey90"),
                    name = NULL, na.value = "grey85") +
  region_layer +
  labs(title = "PUMAs with and without a prison inside their boundary") +
  map_theme
```

```{r}
#| label: map-prison-count
# Number of open state and federal prisons inside each PUMA
puma_geo_l48 %>%
  mutate(n_prisons = cut(num_prisons_in_puma, breaks = c(-Inf, 0, 1, 2, Inf),
                         labels = c("0", "1", "2", "3+"))) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = n_prisons), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("0" = "grey90", "1" = "#fcae91", "2" = "#fb6a4a", "3+" = "#a50f15"),
                    name = "Prisons", na.value = "grey85") +
  region_layer +
  labs(title = "Number of prisons inside each PUMA") +
  map_theme
```

From the maps and the tests below, it is evident that these two are
actually not that different. So I think I should either choose the
number of prisons, since it is the more informative measure, or just
discuss them as a pair of count-based measures, basically in contrast to
the distance-decay group.

### Settlement geography

These are the variables that go into M2 (the model specification, which
includes area/population characteristics).

```{r}
#| label: map-geography
ggplot(puma_geo_l48) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = log_pop_density), colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "log density", option = "cividis", na.value = "grey85") +
  region_layer +
  labs(title = "Population density (log, people per km²)") +
  map_theme

ggplot(puma_geo_l48) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pct_pop_rural), colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "%", option = "cividis", direction = -1, na.value = "grey85") +
  region_layer +
  labs(title = "Share of rural population tracts (RUCA 10)") +
  map_theme

ggplot(puma_geo_l48) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pct_pop_nonmetro), colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "%", option = "cividis", direction = -1, na.value = "grey85") +
  region_layer +
  labs(title = "Share of non-metro population tracts") +
  map_theme
```

### Which PUMAs are selected as rural and as non-metro

A PUMA is selected when more than half of its population lives in that
type of tract.

```{r}
#| label: map-rural-selection
puma_geo_l48 %>%
  mutate(selected = if_else(pct_pop_nonmetro > 50, "Non-metro PUMA", "Not selected")) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = selected), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Non-metro PUMA" = "darkgreen", "Not selected" = "grey90"),
                    name = NULL, na.value = "grey85") +
  region_layer +
  labs(title = "PUMAs with more than 50% of the population in non-metro tracts",
       subtitle = "Non-metro = RUCA 4–10 (micropolitan, small town and rural)") +
  map_theme

puma_geo_l48 %>%
  mutate(selected = if_else(pct_pop_rural > 50, "Rural PUMA", "Not selected")) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = selected), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Rural PUMA" = "darkorange3", "Not selected" = "grey90"),
                    name = NULL, na.value = "grey85") +
  region_layer +
  labs(title = "PUMAs with more than 50% of the population in rural tracts",
       subtitle = "Rural = RUCA 10 only") +
  map_theme

```

Based on this definition, we end up with too few fully rural pumas, so I
think it makes sense to proceed with the non-metro PUMAs and use the
variable pct_pop_nonmetro both in the models and for filtering the rural
subset.

## Correlations

Spearman correlations, since most of the exposure measures are very
skewed.

```{r}
#| label: correlations
cor_vars <- c(
  # Tract-based measures
  "Exposure h=1"             = "prison_exp_h1",
  "Exposure h=5"             = "prison_exp_h5",
  "Exposure h=10"             = "prison_exp_h10",
  "Exposure h=25"            = "prison_exp_h25",
  "Prisons in PUMA"           = "num_prisons_in_puma",
  "Prison in PUMA (0/1)"      = "prison_present_in_puma",
  # Settlement geography
  "Log density"               = "log_pop_density",
  "% rural (RUCA 10)"         = "pct_pop_rural",
  "% non-metro"               = "pct_pop_nonmetro"
)
cor_vars <- cor_vars[cor_vars %in% names(puma_df)]   # skip any that aren't in the data

cor_mat <- puma_df %>%
  select(all_of(cor_vars)) %>%
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman")

# correlation matrix code
cor_long <- as_tibble(cor_mat, rownames = "var1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-var1, names_to = "var2", values_to = "rho") %>%
  mutate(var1 = factor(var1, levels = names(cor_vars)),
         var2 = factor(var2, levels = rev(names(cor_vars))))

ggplot(cor_long, aes(var1, var2, fill = rho)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", rho)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Spearman") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Correlations: exposure measures and settlement geography") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid = element_blank())
```

## Group comparisons

This section shows unadjusted comparisons of the outcomes across
exposure groups. Prison presence gives two groups, and the number of
prisons gives three (0, 1, 2+). Each decay measure is split into an
"unexposed" group (exposure below 0.01, meaning no prison anywhere near
where people live) and four equal-sized groups of the exposed PUMAs.

```{r}
#| label: groupings
puma_groups <- puma_df %>%
  mutate(
    # 1. Any prison inside the PUMA
    grp_presence = factor(if_else(prison_present_in_puma == 1, "Prison in PUMA", "No prison"),
                          levels = c("No prison", "Prison in PUMA")),
    # 2. Number of prisons inside the PUMA
    grp_count = cut(num_prisons_in_puma, breaks = c(-Inf, 0, 1, Inf),
                    labels = c("0", "1", "2+")),
    # 3. Distance-decay exposure: "unexposed" (< 0.01), then quartiles of the exposed PUMAs
    grp_h1  = if_else(prison_exp_h1  < 0.01, "Unexposed",
                      paste0("Q", ntile(if_else(prison_exp_h1  >= 0.01, prison_exp_h1,  NA_real_), 4))),
    grp_h5  = if_else(prison_exp_h5  < 0.01, "Unexposed",
                      paste0("Q", ntile(if_else(prison_exp_h5  >= 0.01, prison_exp_h5,  NA_real_), 4))),
    grp_h10 = if_else(prison_exp_h10 < 0.01, "Unexposed",
                      paste0("Q", ntile(if_else(prison_exp_h10 >= 0.01, prison_exp_h10, NA_real_), 4))),
    grp_h25 = if_else(prison_exp_h25 < 0.01, "Unexposed",
                      paste0("Q", ntile(if_else(prison_exp_h25 >= 0.01, prison_exp_h25, NA_real_), 4))),
    across(c(grp_h1, grp_h5, grp_h10, grp_h25),
           ~ factor(.x, levels = c("Unexposed", "Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"))),
    # For the stratified comparison
    metro = factor(if_else(pct_pop_nonmetro > 50, "Non-metro PUMAs", "Metro PUMAs"))
  )

groupings <- c(
  grp_presence = "Prison inside the PUMA",
  grp_count    = "Number of prisons inside the PUMA",
  grp_h1       = "Decay exposure, h = 1 km",
  grp_h5       = "Decay exposure, h = 5 km",
  grp_h10      = "Decay exposure, h = 10 km",
  grp_h25      = "Decay exposure, h = 25 km"
)

# How many PUMAs in each group
puma_groups %>% count(grp_presence)
puma_groups %>% count(grp_count)
puma_groups %>% count(grp_h1)
puma_groups %>% count(grp_h5)
puma_groups %>% count(grp_h10)
puma_groups %>% count(grp_h25)
```

Mean, median and SD of each outcome in each group:

```{r}
#| label: group-means
# All group labels, in display order
group_levels <- c("No prison", "Prison in PUMA", "0", "1", "2+",
                  "Unexposed", "Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4")

# Long format: one row per PUMA x outcome x grouping
group_long <- puma_groups %>%
  select(GEOID20, all_of(names(outcomes)), all_of(names(groupings))) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(outcomes)), names_to = "y", values_to = "value") %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(groupings)), names_to = "g", values_to = "group",
               values_transform = as.character) %>%
  filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(group)) %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = group_levels))

group_stats <- group_long %>%
  group_by(y, g, group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(value), median = median(value), sd = sd(value),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(outcome  = outcomes[y],
         grouping = factor(groupings[g], levels = groupings))

group_stats %>%
  select(outcome, grouping, group, n, mean, median, sd) %>%
  arrange(outcome, grouping, group) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = c("outcome", "grouping")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(mean, median, sd), decimals = 2) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Outcomes by prison exposure group")
```

The differences in means actually look promising! Pumas with prisons
show higher mean rates of both overdose and divorce than Pumas without
prisons. In addition, the distance-decay measures show that as exposure
increases, the means for both overdose and divorce also increase.

```{r}
#| label: group-tests
# Two groups (prison in PUMA vs not): Welch t-test and Wilcoxon rank-sum test
tests_presence <- group_long %>%
  filter(g == "grp_presence") %>%
  group_by(y, g) %>%
  summarise(
    test_means = "Welch t-test",
    difference = diff(t.test(value ~ droplevels(group))$estimate),   #prison minus no prison
    p_means    = t.test(value ~ droplevels(group))$p.value,
    test_ranks = "Wilcoxon",
    p_ranks    = wilcox.test(value ~ droplevels(group))$p.value,
    p_trend    = NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# More than two ordered groups (count and all decay measures):
# ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis and a linear trend test across the ordered groups
tests_ordered <- group_long %>%
  filter(g != "grp_presence") %>%
  group_by(y, g) %>%
  summarise(
    test_means = "ANOVA",
    difference = NA_real_,
    p_means    = anova(lm(value ~ droplevels(group)))$`Pr(>F)`[1],
    test_ranks = "Kruskal-Wallis",
    p_ranks    = kruskal.test(value ~ droplevels(group))$p.value,
    p_trend    = tidy(lm(value ~ as.integer(droplevels(group))))$p.value[2],   
    .groups = "drop"
  )

test_results <- bind_rows(tests_presence, tests_ordered) %>%
  mutate(outcome  = outcomes[y],
         grouping = factor(groupings[g], levels = groupings)) %>%
  arrange(outcome, grouping) %>%
  select(outcome, grouping, test_means, difference, p_means, test_ranks, p_ranks, p_trend)

test_results %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "outcome") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = difference, decimals = 2) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(p_means, p_ranks, p_trend), decimals = 4) %>%
  sub_missing(missing_text = "") %>%
  cols_label(grouping = "Grouping", test_means = "Means test", difference = "Difference",
             p_means = "p (means)", test_ranks = "Rank test", p_ranks = "p (ranks)",
             p_trend = "p (linear trend)") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Do outcomes differ by prison exposure? (unadjusted)",
subtitle = "Difference = with prison minus without (two-group comparisons only)")
```

These tests check whether the outcomes differ across groups. For the
two-group comparison (prison vs. no prison), we used a Welch t-test for
the means and a Wilcoxon rank-sum test for the whole distributions. For
the groupings with more than two groups, we used ANOVA and
Kruskal-Wallis, plus a linear trend test across the ordered groups.
These tests ignore the controls and assume that PUMAs are independent
(they are not), so they are descriptive only.

### Within metro and non-metro PUMAs

The same prison vs. no prison comparison, separately for metro and
non-metro PUMAs.

```{r}
#| label: group-stratified
# Prison vs. no prison, separately in metro and non-metro PUMAs.
# Welch t-test (means) and Wilcoxon rank-sum test (distributions), as in the main comparison.
stratified <- puma_groups %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(outcomes)), names_to = "y", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(grp_presence)) %>%
  group_by(y, metro) %>%
  summarise(
    n_no_prison    = sum(grp_presence == "No prison"),
    n_prison       = sum(grp_presence == "Prison in PUMA"),
    mean_no_prison = t.test(value ~ grp_presence)$estimate[[1]],
    mean_prison    = t.test(value ~ grp_presence)$estimate[[2]],
    difference     = mean_prison - mean_no_prison,              # prison minus no prison
    p_means        = t.test(value ~ grp_presence)$p.value,
    p_ranks        = wilcox.test(value ~ grp_presence)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(outcome = outcomes[y])

stratified %>%
  select(outcome, metro, n_no_prison, n_prison, mean_no_prison, mean_prison,
         difference, p_means, p_ranks) %>%
  arrange(outcome, metro) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "outcome") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(mean_no_prison, mean_prison, difference), decimals = 2) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(p_means, p_ranks), decimals = 4) %>%
  cols_label(metro = "PUMAs", n_no_prison = "n (no prison)", n_prison = "n (prison)",
             mean_no_prison = "Mean (no prison)", mean_prison = "Mean (prison)",
             difference = "Difference", p_means = "p (t-test)", p_ranks = "p (Wilcoxon)") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Prison vs. no prison, within metro and non-metro PUMAs (unadjusted)")
```

I think this is actually interesting, but unfortunately it contradicts
my initial theory. First of all, there are more prisons in
urban/metropolitan areas (which makes sense given the way we define
metro/non-metro). However, what is more important is that the means are
actually lower (for overdose) or not significantly different (for
divorce) in the rural PUMAs with prisons.

# OLS MODELS

Each model has one exposure measure. Controls are added in stages so we
can see how much the exposure coefficient moves at each step. Standard
errors for all of the models are clustered by state

| Model  | Adds                                                           |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| M1     | nothing (exposure only)                                        |
| M2     | settlement geography: log density, % non-metro, log population |
| M3a    | M2 + economic: % unemployed, log median income                 |
| M3b    | M2 + education: % bachelor's or more                           |
| M3c    | M2 + race: % non-White                                         |
| M3d    | M2 + all of the above                                          |
| M3     | M3d + state fixed effects                                      |
| M3-div | M3d + Census division fixed effects                            |

## Setup and fitting

```{r}
#| label: p4-setup

# Census division for each state (base R state lists; DC added by hand)
state_lookup <- tibble(state = state.abb,
                       division = as.character(state.division)) %>%
  add_row(state = "DC", division = "South Atlantic") %>%
  left_join(distinct(tidycensus::fips_codes, state, state_code), by = "state") %>%
  select(state_fips = state_code, division)

# Exposure measures: variable -> label
exposures <- c(
  prison_exp_h1          = "Exposure, h = 1 km",
  prison_exp_h5          = "Exposure, h = 5 km",
  prison_exp_h10         = "Exposure, h = 10 km",
  prison_exp_h25         = "Exposure, h = 25 km",
  num_prisons_in_puma    = "Number of prisons in PUMA",
  prison_present_in_puma = "Prison in PUMA (0/1)"
)

# Control groups
ctrl_geo  <- c("log_pop_density", "pct_pop_nonmetro", "log_pop")
ctrl_econ <- c("pct_unemployed", "log_medhhinc")
ctrl_educ <- c("pct_bachelors_plus")
ctrl_race <- c("pct_nonwhite")
ctrl_religion <-c("pct_religious")
ctrl_all  <- c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_econ, ctrl_educ, ctrl_race)
ctrl_all_div  <- c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_econ, ctrl_educ, ctrl_race, ctrl_religion)

# Model specifications: one row per stage, with its controls and fixed effects
specs_od <- tibble(
  spec     = c("M1", "M2", "M3a", "M3b", "M3c", "M3d", "M3", "M3-div"),
  controls = list(character(0), ctrl_geo, c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_econ), c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_educ),
                  c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_race), ctrl_all, ctrl_all, ctrl_all),
  fe       = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, "state_fips", "division")
)

specs_div <- tibble(
  spec     = c("M1", "M2", "M3a", "M3b", "M3c", "M3d", "M3", "M3-div"),
  controls = list(character(0), ctrl_geo, c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_econ), c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_educ),
                  c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_race), ctrl_all_div, ctrl_all_div, ctrl_all_div),
  fe       = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, "state_fips", "division")
)

# Both together, with the outcome each set of specs belongs to
specs <- bind_rows(
  specs_od  %>% mutate(y = "overdose_rate_2022_2024"),
  specs_div %>% mutate(y = "pct_divorced_past_yr")
)

# Model data: add division and log distance; standardize continuous exposures
puma_m <- puma_df %>%
  left_join(state_lookup, by = "state_fips") %>%
  mutate(log_dist_nearest = log(dist_nearest_prison_km_popw),
         across(all_of(setdiff(names(exposures), "prison_present_in_puma")),
                ~ (.x - mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))

# One complete-case sample per outcome, using that outcome's own full control set
# (same PUMAs in every model for that outcome)
model_data <- list(
  overdose_rate_2022_2024 = puma_m %>%
    drop_na(all_of(c("overdose_rate_2022_2024", names(exposures), ctrl_all,
                     "state_fips", "division"))),
  pct_divorced_past_yr = puma_m %>%
    drop_na(all_of(c("pct_divorced_past_yr", names(exposures), ctrl_all_div,
                     "state_fips", "division")))
)

map_int(model_data, nrow)   # PUMAs per outcome
```

```{r}
#| label: p4-fit
# Every outcome x specification (its own specs) x exposure, with its formula written out
all_models <- specs %>%
  expand_grid(x = names(exposures)) %>%
  mutate(
    rhs     = map2_chr(x, controls, ~ str_c(c(.x, .y), collapse = " + ")),
    formula = str_c(y, " ~ ", rhs, if_else(is.na(fe), "", str_c(" | ", fe))),
    model   = map2(formula, y, ~ feols(as.formula(.x), data = model_data[[.y]],
                                       cluster = ~state_fips))
  )

all_models %>% distinct(y, spec, formula)   # check: the divorce M3d/M3/M3-div should include the extra controls

# Pull out the exposure coefficient from each model
results <- all_models %>%
  mutate(
    coef = map2(model, x, ~ tidy(.x, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
                              filter(term == .y) %>%
                              select(estimate, std.error, p.value, conf.low, conf.high)),
    r2 = map_dbl(model, ~ r2(.x, "r2")),
    n  = map_int(model, nobs)
  ) %>%
  select(y, x, spec, coef, r2, n) %>%
  unnest(coef) %>%
    mutate(spec = factor(spec, levels = specs_od$spec)) %>%
  group_by(y, x) %>%
  arrange(spec, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(pct_change_from_M1 = 100 * (estimate - first(estimate)) / abs(first(estimate))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(outcome  = outcomes[y],
         exposure = factor(exposures[x], levels = exposures))
```

## All stages, by exposure

Each table is one exposure measure across all model stages, so we can
see how β, its standard error and R² change as controls are added.

## All exposure measures

```{r}
#| label: p4-summary-table
results %>%
  filter(spec %in% c("M1", "M2", "M3d", "M3", "M3-div")) %>%
  select(outcome, exposure, spec, estimate, std.error, p.value, pct_change_from_M1, r2) %>%
  arrange(outcome, exposure, spec) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = c("outcome", "exposure")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(estimate, std.error, r2), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = p.value, decimals = 4) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = pct_change_from_M1, decimals = 0) %>%
  sub_missing(missing_text = "") %>%
  cols_label(spec = "Model", estimate = "β", std.error = "SE (state)", p.value = "p",
             pct_change_from_M1 = "% change vs M1", r2 = "R²") %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"), locations = cells_body(rows = p.value < 0.05)) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Prison exposure coefficient across model stages",
             subtitle = "Continuous exposures per SD; presence = with vs. without; SEs clustered by state. Shaded: p < 0.05")
```

OLS shows an effect on the divorce rate, which seems to be stronger at
lower h. The effect of prisons on overdose is only significant with the
distance-decay measure at h = 1 and with both count-based measures.

## Change in exposure coefficient as controls are added

```{r}
#| label: stepwise-h5
# three versions: overdose; divorce with total religious adherence; divorce with the four religious families instead. Controls are added one per step (cumulative), then state FE

ctrl_relig_families <- c("pct_evangelical", "pct_catholic", "pct_mainline", "pct_black_protestant")

ctrl_order <- list(
  overdose         = c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_econ, ctrl_educ, ctrl_race),
  divorce_total    = c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_econ, ctrl_educ, ctrl_race, "pct_religious"),
  divorce_families = c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_econ, ctrl_educ, ctrl_race, ctrl_relig_families)
)

# outcome for each version
y_of <- c(overdose         = "overdose_rate_2022_2024",
          divorce_total    = "pct_divorced_past_yr",
          divorce_families = "pct_divorced_past_yr")

ctrl_names <- c(log_pop_density      = "Log population density",
                pct_pop_nonmetro     = "% population in non-metro tracts",
                log_pop              = "Log population",
                pct_unemployed       = "% unemployed",
                log_medhhinc         = "Log median household income",
                pct_bachelors_plus   = "% bachelor's degree or higher",
                pct_nonwhite         = "% non-white",
                pct_religious        = "% religious adherents (all)",
                pct_evangelical      = "% evangelical Protestant",
                pct_catholic         = "% Catholic",
                pct_mainline         = "% mainline Protestant",
                pct_black_protestant = "% Black Protestant")

x_step <- "prison_exp_h5"  

# one row per step: the controls included so far, then a final step with state FE
stepwise <- imap_dfr(ctrl_order, ~ tibble(
    version  = .y,
    y        = y_of[[.y]],
    step     = 0:(length(.x) + 1),
    added    = c("Exposure only", ctrl_names[.x], "State fixed effects"),
    controls = c(list(character(0)), accumulate(.x, c), list(.x)),
    fe       = c(rep(NA_character_, length(.x) + 1), "state_fips")
  )) %>%
  mutate(
    formula = pmap_chr(list(y, controls, fe),
                       ~ str_c(..1, " ~ ", str_c(c(x_step, ..2), collapse = " + "),
                               if_else(is.na(..3), "", str_c(" | ", ..3)))),
    model   = map2(formula, y, ~ feols(as.formula(.x), data = model_data[[.y]],
                                       cluster = ~state_fips)),
    coef    = map(model, ~ tidy(.x, conf.int = TRUE) %>% filter(term == x_step)),
    r2      = map_dbl(model, ~ r2(.x, "r2")),
    n       = map_int(model, nobs)
  ) %>%
  unnest(coef) %>%
  group_by(version) %>%
  mutate(change_prev = estimate - lag(estimate),               
         pct_from_m1 = 100 * (estimate - first(estimate)) / abs(first(estimate))) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#| label: stepwise-h5-overdose

# overdose table
stepwise %>%
  filter(version == "overdose") %>%
  select(step, added, estimate, std.error, p.value, conf.low, conf.high, change_prev, pct_from_m1, r2) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(step = "Step", added = "Added", estimate = "β", std.error = "SE", p.value = "p",
             conf.low = "95% CI low", conf.high = "95% CI high",
             change_prev = "Change from previous step", pct_from_m1 = "% change from step 0",
             r2 = "R²") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, change_prev), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = p.value, decimals = 4) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = pct_from_m1, decimals = 1) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = r2, decimals = 3) %>%
  sub_missing(missing_text = "") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Overdose deaths per 100,000: exposure coefficient as controls are added one at a time")
```

# DISTANCE BANDS ANALYSIS/TEST

This was my attempt to illustrate how the effect fades as distance
increases. We can see that the effect of prisons on overdose is close to
zero at distances of more than 5 km. For divorce, we can see a big drop
in the coefficient when the distance increases from 2 km to 5 km, and it
continues to decrease as the distance increases.

```{r}
#| label: ring-models

#distance rings
rings <- c("ring_0_2", "ring_2_5", "ring_5_10", "ring_10_25", "ring_25_50")

ring_labels <- c(ring_0_2 = "0–2 km", ring_2_5 = "2–5 km", ring_5_10 = "5–10 km",
                 ring_10_25 = "10–25 km", ring_25_50 = "25–50 km")

# M3 formula for each outcome (its own controls + state FE), with the exposure swapped for all the rings
ring_models <- all_models %>%
  filter(spec == "M3", x == "prison_exp_h10") %>%
  distinct(y, formula) %>%
  mutate(
    formula = str_replace(formula, "prison_exp_h10", paste(rings, collapse = " + ")),
    model   = map2(formula, y,
                   ~ feols(as.formula(.x), data = model_data[[.y]], cluster = ~ state_fips))
  )

ring_models %>% pull(model) %>% etable()
```

```{r}
#| label: ring-n

# how many PUMAs have any prison in each ring 
ring_n <- model_data[["overdose_rate_2022_2024"]] %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(rings), ~ sum(.x > 0))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "term", values_to = "n_pumas")

ring_n
```

```{r}
#| label: ring-plot
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.5

# axis labels with the number of PUMAs under each ring
ring_axis <- ring_n %>%
  mutate(axis_label = paste0(ring_labels[term], "\n(n = ", n_pumas, ")")) %>%
  pull(axis_label)

outcome_panels <- c(overdose_rate_2022_2024 = "Overdose deaths per 100,000",
                    pct_divorced_past_yr    = "Divorced in past year (percentage points)")

ring_models %>%
  mutate(coefs = map(model, ~ tidy(.x, conf.int = TRUE))) %>%
  select(y, coefs) %>%
  unnest(coefs) %>%
  filter(term %in% rings) %>%
  left_join(ring_n, by = "term") %>%
  mutate(ring    = factor(paste0(ring_labels[term], "\n(n = ", n_pumas, ")"),
                          levels = ring_axis),
         outcome = factor(outcome_panels[y], levels = outcome_panels)) %>%   
  ggplot(aes(x = ring, y = estimate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high)) +
  facet_wrap(~ outcome, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Distance from where residents live (n = PUMAs with any prison in the ring)",
       y = "Change with one more prison in the ring",
       title = "Prisons at different distances, M3 with state fixed effects",
       caption = paste("Points: OLS coefficients; bars: 95% confidence intervals (SEs clustered by state).",
                       "All rings are in the same model, with the M3 controls for each outcome.",
                       "Units differ by panel: deaths per 100,000 (overdose), percentage points (divorce).",
                       sep = "\n")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0))
```

# LOCAL MEASURES (h=1,5)

```{r}
#| label: fig-influence-dist
#| fig-height: 4

# one row per PUMA x outcome x exposure (raw exposure)
local_long <- puma_df %>%
  select(GEOID20, all_of(names(outcomes)), prison_exp_h1, prison_exp_h5) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(outcomes)), names_to = "y", values_to = "value_y") %>%
  pivot_longer(c(prison_exp_h1, prison_exp_h5), names_to = "x", values_to = "exposure") %>%
  drop_na(value_y) %>%
  mutate(h = exposures[x], outcome = outcomes[y])

# histogram
local_long %>%
  distinct(GEOID20, h, exposure) %>%
  ggplot(aes(exposure)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "grey40") +
  scale_x_sqrt() +
  facet_wrap(~ h, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Exposure (square-root scale)", y = "PUMAs",
       title = "Local exposure: most PUMAs are near zero") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Both distributions are skewed to the right, even on a square-root scale, which confirms the issue identified earlier: very few PUMAs have high exposure on the very local measures, especially h = 1 km (however, this is expected, because at h = 1 km exposure falls off so quickly with distance)

```{r}
#| label: fig-exposure-scatter-all
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6.5

all_long <- model_data %>%
  imap_dfr(~ .x %>%
             select(GEOID20, value_y = all_of(.y), all_of(names(h_vars))) %>%
             mutate(y = .y)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(h_vars)), names_to = "x", values_to = "exposure") %>%
  mutate(h       = factor(h_vars[x], levels = h_vars),         # keep h = 1, 5, 10, 25 in order
         outcome = factor(outcomes[y], levels = outcomes))

ggplot(all_long, aes(exposure, value_y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, colour = "#B23A1E", linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(outcome ~ h, scales = "free", labeller = label_wrap_gen(25)) +
  labs(x = "Exposure (SD)", y = NULL,
       title = "Outcome vs. prison exposure, all decay distances (no controls)",
       caption = "Black: straight line; red: loess smooth.") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The relationship between prison exposure and divorce can be described as linear. Even though the straight and smoothed lines diverge for some of the exposure measures, the relationship becomes more linear once the GAM accounts for the controls.

The relationship between prison exposure and overdose is not linear: the slope is largely driven by a few urban PUMAs with both very high exposure and very high overdose rates, which is also supported by the Cook’s distance and GAM results below.


## Cook's distance

```{r}
#| label: influence-setup
# control strings for each outcome
ctrl_str <- c(overdose_rate_2022_2024 = str_c(ctrl_all,     collapse = " + "),
              pct_divorced_past_yr    = str_c(ctrl_all_div, collapse = " + "))

# exposures (h = 1, 5 and 10 km)
infl_x <- c("prison_exp_h1", "prison_exp_h5", "prison_exp_h10")

# fit M3 for every outcome x exposure pair (2 x 3 = 6 models)
infl_models <- expand_grid(y = names(outcomes), x = infl_x) %>%
  mutate(
    # write the formula as text: outcome ~ exposure + controls + state dummies
    formula = str_c(y, " ~ ", x, " + ", ctrl_str[y], " + factor(state_fips)"),
    # fit the model on the sample for that outcome
    model   = map2(formula, y, ~ lm(as.formula(.x), data = model_data[[.y]])),
    # get Cook's distance and leverage for each PUMA, keep only the columns I need
    infl    = map2(model, y, ~ augment(.x, data = model_data[[.y]]) %>%
                     select(GEOID20, name = NAMELSAD20, state = STUSPS20,
                            all_of(infl_x), cooks = .cooksd, leverage = .hat) %>%
                     mutate(row = row_number())),
    # usual cutoff for "influential": Cook's distance above 4/n
    cutoff  = map_dbl(model, ~ 4 / nobs(.x))
  )

# one long table
infl_long <- infl_models %>%
  select(y, x, cutoff, infl) %>%
  unnest(infl) %>%
  mutate(exposure_z = case_when(x == "prison_exp_h1"  ~ prison_exp_h1,
                                x == "prison_exp_h5"  ~ prison_exp_h5,
                                x == "prison_exp_h10" ~ prison_exp_h10),
         outcome    = outcomes[y],
         h          = exposures[x]) %>%
  select(-all_of(infl_x))

# summary for each model
infl_long %>%
  group_by(outcome, h) %>%
  summarise(n_flagged = sum(cooks > cutoff),
            share_flagged = mean(cooks > cutoff),
            top10_share_of_total_cooks = sum(sort(cooks, decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]) / sum(cooks),
            .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
#| label: influence-refit
# refit M3 (feols, clustered SEs) on: all PUMAs; without PUMAs above 4/n; without the top 1% of exposure
flagged <- infl_long %>% filter(cooks > cutoff) %>% distinct(y, x, GEOID20)

infl_grid <- expand_grid(y = names(outcomes), x = infl_x)

influence_samples <- bind_rows(
  infl_grid %>%
    mutate(sample = "All PUMAs",
           data   = map(y, ~ model_data[[.x]])),
  infl_grid %>%
    mutate(sample = "Without Cook's D > 4/n",
           data   = map2(y, x, ~ anti_join(model_data[[.x]],
                                           flagged[flagged$y == .x & flagged$x == .y, ],
                                           by = "GEOID20"))),
  infl_grid %>%
    mutate(sample = "Without top 1% exposure",
           data   = map2(y, x, ~ model_data[[.x]][model_data[[.x]][[.y]] <=
                                                    quantile(model_data[[.x]][[.y]], 0.99), ]))
)

influence_check <- influence_samples %>%
  mutate(
    model = pmap(list(y, x, data), ~ feols(as.formula(str_c(..1, " ~ ", ..2, " + ", ctrl_str[..1],
                                                              " | state_fips")),
                                           data = ..3, cluster = ~state_fips)),
    n     = map_int(model, nobs),
    coef  = map2(model, x, ~ tidy(.x, conf.int = TRUE) %>% filter(term == .y))
  ) %>%
  select(y, x, sample, n, coef) %>%
  unnest(coef) %>%
  mutate(outcome = outcomes[y], h = exposures[x],
         sample  = factor(sample, levels = c("All PUMAs", "Without Cook's D > 4/n",
                                             "Without top 1% exposure"))) %>%
  arrange(outcome, h, sample)

influence_check %>%
  select(outcome, h, sample, n, estimate, std.error, p.value) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = c("outcome", "h")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(estimate, std.error), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = p.value, decimals = 4) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Prison coefficient with and without influential PUMAs")
```

Based on the Cook's distance check, the divorce results are not very affected by influential PUMAs (the coefficient stays similar and significant when the influential PUMAs or the 1% most exposed PUMAs are removed). The overdose results are the opposite. At h = 1 km, the coefficient stays positive when the influential PUMAs are removed, but it drops to almost zero when the 25 most exposed PUMAs are removed, so these 25 PUMAs drive the relationship(?). At h = 5 and 10 km the relationship was not significant in the first place, and it disappears in both samples, where outliers/flagged PUMAs are removed.

```{r}
# PUMAs in the top 1% of exposure, for each h (overdose sample)
od_mean <- mean(model_data[["overdose_rate_2022_2024"]]$overdose_rate_2022_2024)

top1 <- puma_df %>%
  semi_join(model_data[["overdose_rate_2022_2024"]], by = "GEOID20") %>%
  # overdose percentile among all PUMAs (before keeping only the top 1%)
  mutate(od_percentile = round(100 * percent_rank(overdose_rate_2022_2024))) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(infl_x), names_to = "x", values_to = "exposure") %>%
  group_by(x) %>%
  filter(exposure >= quantile(exposure, 0.99)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(h = factor(exposures[x], levels = exposures))

# how many of them are high-overdose (top quarter) and how many are rural
top1 %>%
  group_by(h) %>%
  summarise(n_pumas         = n(),
            n_high_overdose = sum(od_percentile > 75),
            mean_overdose   = mean(overdose_rate_2022_2024),
            n_rural         = sum(pct_pop_nonmetro > 50))

# the list
top1 %>%
  arrange(h, desc(overdose_rate_2022_2024)) %>%
  select(h, NAMELSAD20, STUSPS20, exposure, overdose_rate_2022_2024, od_percentile,
         pct_pop_nonmetro) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "h") %>%
  cols_label(NAMELSAD20 = "PUMA", STUSPS20 = "State", exposure = "Exposure (raw)",
             overdose_rate_2022_2024 = "Overdose rate", od_percentile = "Overdose percentile",
             pct_pop_nonmetro = "% non-metro") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(exposure, overdose_rate_2022_2024, pct_pop_nonmetro), decimals = 1) %>%
  tab_header(title = "PUMAs in the top 1% of prison exposure",
             subtitle = str_c("Overdose deaths per 100,000; national mean = ", round(od_mean, 1)))
```

The list above shows the 25 PUMAs with the highest exposure (for each h), which largely drive the overdose relationship in the national model. Most of them are geographically concentrated in the Northeast, and all of them are urban!

# INTERACTIONS: Rural vs. urban and South vs. the rest

```{r}
#| label: interaction-setup
# add a dummy
# rural = 1 if more than half the population lives in non-metro tracts
model_data <- map(model_data, ~ .x %>%
                    mutate(rural = as.integer(pct_pop_nonmetro > 50),
                           south = as.integer(state_fips %in% south_fips)))

int_x <- names(exposures)   # exposure = all decay distances

map(model_data, ~ count(.x, rural))   # how many PUMAs in each group
```

## Rural vs. urban

```{r}
#| label: rural-models

#table with coefficients foe all exposure measures
rural_models <- expand_grid(y = names(outcomes), x = int_x) %>%
  mutate(
    formula = str_c(y, " ~ ", x, " * rural + ", ctrl_str[y], " | state_fips"),
    model   = map2(formula, y, ~ feols(as.formula(.x), data = model_data[[.y]],
                                       cluster = ~state_fips)),
    # Slope of exposure separately for urban (0) and rural (1) PUMAs
    slopes  = pmap(list(model, x, y), ~ avg_slopes(..1, variables = ..2, by = "rural",
                                                   newdata = model_data[[..3]]) %>%
                     as_tibble() %>%
                     select(rural, estimate, std.error, p.value, conf.low, conf.high)),
    # Test of the difference = the interaction coefficient
    diff    = map2(model, x, ~ tidy(.x) %>% filter(term == str_c(.y, ":rural")) %>%
                     select(diff = estimate, diff_p = p.value))
  )

rural_results <- rural_models %>%
  select(y, x, slopes, diff) %>%
  unnest(slopes) %>%
  unnest(diff) %>%
  mutate(outcome = factor(outcomes[y], levels = outcomes),
         h       = factor(exposures[x], levels = exposures),
         group   = if_else(rural == 1, "Rural", "Urban"))

rural_results %>%
  select(outcome, h, group, estimate, std.error, p.value, diff, diff_p) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "outcome") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(estimate, std.error, diff), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(p.value, diff_p), decimals = 4) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Prison slope for rural and urban PUMAs (full sample, interaction)",
             subtitle = "diff = rural − urban slope; diff_p = test that they are equal")
```

The table above shows the prison slope for each exposure measure and its significance in urban and rural PUMAs. For overdose, the rural slope is larger than the urban one for all of the exposures and is statistically significant for three out of four of them (at h = 25 km, p = 0.08). However, the difference between the urban and rural slopes is not statistically significant.

For divorce, the situation is the opposite. The association between prison exposure and divorce is stronger in urban PUMAs, while in rural PUMAs the slope becomes negative and is not significant.

The tables below show the full models for each exposure:

```{r}
#| label: rural-h1-tables
# tables for the exposure × rural model, h = 1 km
term_lab <- c(prison_exp_h1         = "Prison exposure, h = 1 km (per 1 SD)",
              rural                 = "Rural PUMA (1 = rural)",
              `prison_exp_h5:rural` = "Exposure × rural",
              log_pop_density       = "Log population density",
              pct_pop_nonmetro      = "% population in non-metro tracts",
              log_pop               = "Log population",
              pct_unemployed        = "% unemployed",
              log_medhhinc          = "Log median household income",
              pct_bachelors_plus    = "% bachelor's degree or more",
              pct_nonwhite          = "% nonwhite",
              pct_religious         = "% religious adherents")

rural_h1 <- rural_models %>%
  filter(x == "prison_exp_h1") %>%
  mutate(
    # every coefficient in the model
    coefs  = map(model, ~ tidy(.x, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
                   select(-statistic) %>%
                   mutate(part = "Coefficients",
                          term = coalesce(term_lab[term], term))),
    # the prison slope for urban and rural PUMAs (from avg_slopes)
    groups = map(slopes, ~ .x %>%
                   mutate(part = "Prison slope by group",
                          term = if_else(rural == 1, "Slope in rural PUMAs",
                                                     "Slope in urban PUMAs")) %>%
                   select(-rural)),
    # model information
    fit    = map(model, ~ tibble(part = "Model",
                                 term = c("PUMAs", "States (fixed effects)", "Within R²"),
                                 estimate = c(nobs(.x), .x$fixef_sizes[["state_fips"]],
                                              r2(.x, "wr2")))),
    #ci written as text here, so the model rows just stay empty
    rows   = pmap(list(coefs, groups, fit), ~ bind_rows(..1, ..2, ..3) %>%
                    mutate(ci = if_else(is.na(conf.low), NA_character_,
                                        sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", conf.low, conf.high))) %>%
                    select(part, term, estimate, std.error, p.value, ci)),
    tab    = map2(rows, y, ~ .x %>%
                    gt(groupname_col = "part", rowname_col = "term") %>%
                    fmt_number(columns = c(estimate, std.error), decimals = 3) %>%
                    fmt_number(columns = p.value, decimals = 4) %>%
                    fmt_number(columns = estimate,
                               rows = term %in% c("PUMAs", "States (fixed effects)"),
                               decimals = 0) %>%
                    sub_missing(missing_text = "") %>%
                    cols_label(estimate = "Estimate", std.error = "SE", p.value = "p",
                               ci = "95% CI") %>%
                    tab_header(title = outcomes[.y],
                               subtitle = "Exposure × rural, h = 1 km, state fixed effects") %>%
                    tab_source_note("SEs clustered by state. Exposure standardized nationally (mean 0, SD 1)."))
  )

rural_h1$tab[[1]]   # overdose
rural_h1$tab[[2]]   # divorce
```

Prison exposure, h = 1 km - the prison exposure slope for urban PUMAs only
Rural PUMA - how much higher overdose is in a rural PUMA than in urban one at average exposure(?)
prison_exp_h1:rural (Exposure × rural) - how much steeper the prison exposure slope is in rural PUMAs than in urban ones.
Slope in urban PUMAs = Prison exposure, h = 1 km
Slope in Rural PUMAs = Prison exposure, h = 1 km + prison_exp_h1:rural (Exposure × rural)

### test

This is the same setup, but with the 25 most exposed PUMAs removed. The urban slope drops considerably, while the rural slope stays large and significant.

```{r}

#| label: rural-trim-check
# Rural interaction with and without the top 1% of exposure (by measure)
# The top 1% PUMAs are all urban, so this shows whether they drive the urban slope
trim_grid <- expand_grid(y = names(outcomes), x = int_x)

rural_trim <- bind_rows(
  trim_grid %>%
    mutate(sample = "All PUMAs",
           data   = map(y, ~ model_data[[.x]])),
  trim_grid %>%
    mutate(sample = "Without top 1% exposure",
           data   = map2(y, x, ~ model_data[[.x]][model_data[[.x]][[.y]] <=
                                                    quantile(model_data[[.x]][[.y]], 0.99), ]))
) %>%
  mutate(
    model  = pmap(list(y, x, data), ~ feols(as.formula(str_c(..1, " ~ ", ..2, " * rural + ",
                                                               ctrl_str[..1], " | state_fips")),
                                            data = ..3, cluster = ~state_fips)),
    # urban and rural slopes
    slopes = pmap(list(model, x, data), ~ avg_slopes(..1, variables = ..2, by = "rural",
                                                     newdata = ..3) %>%
                    as_tibble() %>%
                    select(rural, estimate, p.value)),
    # the gap (interaction) and its test
    diff   = map2(model, x, ~ tidy(.x) %>% filter(term == str_c(.y, ":rural")) %>%
                    select(diff = estimate, diff_p = p.value)),
    n      = map_int(model, nobs)
  )

rural_trim %>%
  select(y, x, sample, n, slopes, diff) %>%
  unnest(slopes) %>%
  unnest(diff) %>%
  mutate(outcome = outcomes[y],
         h       = factor(exposures[x], levels = exposures),
         group   = if_else(rural == 1, "rural", "urban")) %>%
  select(outcome, h, sample, n, group, estimate, p.value, diff, diff_p) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = c(estimate, p.value)) %>%
  select(outcome, h, sample, n, estimate_urban, p.value_urban,
         estimate_rural, p.value_rural, diff, diff_p) %>%
  arrange(outcome, h, sample) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "outcome") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(estimate_urban, estimate_rural, diff), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = starts_with("p.value") | matches("diff_p"), decimals = 4) %>%
  cols_label(estimate_urban = "Urban slope", p.value_urban = "p",
             estimate_rural = "Rural slope", p.value_rural = "p",
             diff = "Gap", diff_p = "p (gap)") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Rural vs. urban prison slope, with and without the top 1% of exposure")
```


# NONLINEARITY (GAM)

A GAM (generalized additive model) lets the data choose the shape, instead of forcing linear relationship like OLS (edf ≈ 1 => the relationship is basically a
straight line, while larger values mean it bends)

```{r}
#| label: gam-models
gam_models <- expand_grid(y = names(outcomes), x = infl_x) %>%
  mutate(
    formula = str_c(y, " ~ s(", x, ", k = 5) + ", ctrl_str[y], " + factor(state_fips)"),
    model   = map2(formula, y, ~ gam(as.formula(.x), data = model_data[[.y]], method = "REML")),
    smooth  = map(model, ~ summary(.x)$s.table %>% as_tibble(rownames = "term"))
  )

gam_models %>%
  select(y, x, smooth) %>%
  unnest(smooth) %>%
  transmute(outcome = outcomes[y], h = exposures[x], edf, F, p_value = `p-value`) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "outcome") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(edf, F), decimals = 2) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = p_value, decimals = 4) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Smooth of prison exposure (GAM with M3 controls and state FE)",
             subtitle = "edf ≈ 1: linear; larger edf: curved")
```

The GAM confirms that the relationship between prison exposure and divorce is linear, while the relationship between prison exposure and overdose is not. The overdose relationship also seems to become increasingly nonlinear as h increases.

```{r}
#| label: fig-gam-smooths
#| fig-height: 7
# the estimated smooth for each model (partial effect, with 95% band and data rug)
par(mfrow = c(2, 3))
walk2(gam_models$model,
      str_c(str_trunc(outcomes[gam_models$y], 25), ", ", exposures[gam_models$x]),
      ~ plot(.x, select = 1, shade = TRUE, rug = TRUE, main = .y,
             xlab = "Exposure (SD)", ylab = "Partial effect"))
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

# SPATIAL DIAGNOSTICS

OLS assumes that PUMAs are independent of each other. But if neighboring pumas have similar residuals, this assumption doesn’t hold: the standard errors are wrong, and the model is missing something regional. Here we check this for M3 (all controls + state fixed effects) with all six exposure measures.

The neighbors are defined in two ways, to see if the choice matters:

Queen contiguity: PUMAs that share a border or a corner. Two PUMAs (islands) have no neighbors. 
6 nearest neighbors: every PUMA gets six neighbors, no matter its size.

```{r}
#| label: spatial-setup

spatial_exposures <- exposures  

# Model data with boundaries, one per outcome
# Rows stay in this order for the models, the weights, and the maps.
geo_data <- map(names(outcomes),
                ~ puma_geo %>%
                    select(GEOID20) %>%
                    st_transform(5070) %>%
                    inner_join(model_data[[.x]], by = "GEOID20")) %>%
  set_names(names(outcomes))

# Queen contiguity: PUMAs that share a border or corner are neighbors
# (snap = 1 m bridges tiny gaps between cartographic boundaries)
queen_nb <- map(geo_data, ~ poly2nb(.x, queen = TRUE, snap = 1))

# 6 nearest neighbors, measured from a point inside each PUMA
knn_nb <- map(geo_data, ~ .x %>%
                            st_geometry() %>%
                            st_point_on_surface() %>%
                            st_coordinates() %>%
                            knearneigh(k = 6) %>%
                            knn2nb())

# Row-standardized weights, stored as weights[[outcome]]$queen / $knn
weights <- map2(queen_nb, knn_nb,
                ~ list(queen    = nb2listw(.x, style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE),
                       knn      = nb2listw(.y, style = "W"),
                       queen_nb = .x))

```

```{r}
#| label: p5-models
# M3 for each outcome and exposure, refitted with lm() so the spatial tests can use it.
# The formulas come from Phase 4 (so each outcome keeps its own controls);
# only the fixed effects are written as state dummies, which lm() needs.
p5_models <- all_models %>%
  filter(spec == "M3", x %in% names(spatial_exposures)) %>%
  mutate(formula_lm = str_replace(formula, " \\| state_fips", " + factor(state_fips)"),
         model      = map2(formula_lm, y,
                           ~ lm(as.formula(.x), data = st_drop_geometry(geo_data[[.y]])))) %>%
  select(y, x, formula_lm, model)

# sanity check: the exposure coefficients match the Phase 4 feols M3 results
p5_models %>%
  mutate(estimate_lm = map2_dbl(model, x, ~ coef(.x)[[.y]])) %>%
  left_join(results %>% filter(spec == "M3") %>% select(y, x, estimate_feols = estimate),
            by = c("y", "x")) %>%
  select(y, x, estimate_lm, estimate_feols)
```

## Moran's I on the outcome and on the residuals

```{r}
#| label: p5-moran
# Clustering of the outcome itself
moran_results <- expand_grid(y = names(outcomes), w = c("queen", "knn")) %>%
  mutate(
    outcome_test = map2(y, w, ~ moran.test(geo_data[[.x]][[.x]], weights[[.x]][[.y]],
                                           zero.policy = TRUE)),
    outcome_I = map_dbl(outcome_test, ~ unname(.x$estimate[1])),
    outcome_p = map_dbl(outcome_test, ~ .x$p.value)
  ) %>%
  select(-outcome_test)

# Clustering of what the M3 model leaves unexplained
residual_moran <- p5_models %>%
  expand_grid(w = c("queen", "knn")) %>%
  mutate(
    lw         = map2(y, w, ~ weights[[.x]][[.y]]),
    test       = map2(model, lw, ~ lm.morantest(.x, .y, zero.policy = TRUE)),
    residual_I = map_dbl(test, ~ unname(.x$estimate[1])),
    residual_p = map_dbl(test, ~ .x$p.value)
  ) %>%
  select(y, x, w, residual_I, residual_p)

residual_moran %>%
  left_join(moran_results, by = c("y", "w")) %>%
  mutate(outcome  = outcomes[y],
         exposure = spatial_exposures[x],
         weights  = if_else(w == "queen", "Queen contiguity", "6 nearest neighbors")) %>%
  select(outcome, weights, exposure, outcome_I, residual_I, residual_p) %>%
  arrange(outcome, weights) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = c("outcome", "weights")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(outcome_I, residual_I), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = residual_p, decimals = 4) %>%
  cols_label(exposure = "Model (M3) with", outcome_I = "Moran's I: outcome",
             residual_I = "Moran's I: M3 residuals", residual_p = "p (residuals)") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Spatial clustering before and after the model")
```

Based on Moran’s I, overdose rates are strongly clustered, both for the outcome itself and for the residuals. This clustering might be real, but given the way the puma overdose rates were produced, it may partly be an
artifact of the data. This is also supported by Moran’s I for suicide rates, which also come from the CDC and show even stronger clustering. This suggests that the way the data are constructed may produce artificial clustering.

# SPATIAL MODELS

| Model | Assumes | Role here |
|------------------|-------------------------------------|------------------|
| SEM | nearby PUMAs share unmeasured conditions, so their errors are correlated | main spatial model |
| SDEM | SEM + exposure in neighboring PUMAs can matter too | do prisons just outside a PUMA matter? |

Both keep the full M3 specification (each outcome with its own controls). They're estimated by maximum likelihood, so the standard errors are model-based, not clustered.

## Setup

The spatial models need neighbor relations to go both ways, so the kNN weights were made symmetric: two pumas are neighbors if either one is among the other’s 6 nearest. Because of this, some PUMAs end up with a few more than six neighbors.

```{r}
#| label: p6-setup

weight_labels <- c(queen = "Queen", knn = "kNN (k = 6)")

# Weights for the spatial models. kNN is made symmetric (neighbors if either PUMA is among
# the other's 6 nearest), which the exact eigenvalue method requires. Queen is already symmetric.
p6_weights <- map(weights, ~ list(queen = .x$queen,
                                  knn   = nb2listw(make.sym.nb(.x$knn$neighbours), style = "W")))

# Eigenvalues of each weights matrix, computed once and reused by every model.
# similar.listw() gives an equivalent symmetric matrix, so the eigenvalues are real.
p6_eig <- map(p6_weights, ~ list(queen = eigenw(similar.listw(.x$queen)),
                                 knn   = eigenw(similar.listw(.x$knn))))
```

## SEM and SDEM, all exposure measures

```{r}
#| label: p6-fit-error-models
# Slow (2 outcomes x 6 exposures x 2 weight matrices x 2 models), so this is run by hand
# once and the fitted models are saved; the next chunk reads them.
# Formulas: the M3 formulas from Phase 5 (each outcome keeps its own controls).
# "eigen" computes exact standard errors from the precomputed eigenvalues.

#                ~ errorsarlm(as.formula(..1), data = st_drop_geometry(geo_data[[..2]]),
#                             listw = p6_weights[[..2]][[..3]],
#                             Durbin = as.formula(paste("~", ..4)),   # lag only the exposure
#                             method = "eigen",
#                             control = list(pre_eig = p6_eig[[..2]][[..3]]),
#                             zero.policy = TRUE),
#                .progress = "SDEM")
#  ) %>%
#  saveRDS("data/final/p6_error_models.rds")
```

```{r}
#| label: p6-load-error-models
error_models <- readRDS("data/final/p6_error_models.rds")
```

```{r}
#| label: p6-extract-error-models
error_results <- error_models %>%
  mutate(
    # SEM: the exposure coefficient
    sem_coef = map2(sem, x, ~ as_tibble(summary(.x)$Coef, rownames = "term") %>%
                               filter(term == .y) %>%
                               transmute(estimate = Estimate, std.error = `Std. Error`,
                                         p.value = `Pr(>|z|)`)),
    sem_lambda = map_dbl(sem, ~ .x$lambda),
    sem_aic    = map_dbl(sem, AIC),

    # SDEM direct: exposure in the PUMA itself
    sdem_direct = map2(sdem, x, ~ as_tibble(summary(.x)$Coef, rownames = "term") %>%
                                   filter(term == .y) %>%
                                   transmute(estimate = Estimate, std.error = `Std. Error`,
                                             p.value = `Pr(>|z|)`)),
    # SDEM indirect: exposure in neighboring PUMAs (the "lag." term)
    sdem_indirect = map2(sdem, x, ~ as_tibble(summary(.x)$Coef, rownames = "term") %>%
                                     filter(term == paste0("lag.", .y)) %>%
                                     transmute(estimate = Estimate, std.error = `Std. Error`,
                                               p.value = `Pr(>|z|)`)),
    # SDEM total = direct + indirect; its SE uses the covariance between the two
    sdem_total = map2(sdem, x, ~ tibble(
                   estimate  = sum(coef(.x)[c(.y, paste0("lag.", .y))]),
                   std.error = sqrt(sum(vcov(.x)[c(.y, paste0("lag.", .y)),
                                                 c(.y, paste0("lag.", .y))]))) %>%
                   mutate(p.value = 2 * pnorm(-abs(estimate / std.error)))),
    sdem_lambda = map_dbl(sdem, ~ .x$lambda),
    sdem_aic    = map_dbl(sdem, AIC)
  ) %>%
  select(-sem, -sdem)

# OLS M3 (state-clustered) from Phase 4, for comparison
ols_m3 <- results %>%
  filter(spec == "M3") %>%
  select(y, x, ols_estimate = estimate, ols_se = std.error, ols_p = p.value)
```

## One exposure in detail: OLS vs. SEM vs. SDEM

Set `main_x` at the top of the chunk to choose the exposure. It's also used by the model checks below.

```{r}
#| label: p6-main-table
# One comparison table: OLS M3 vs. SEM vs. SDEM for the main exposure,
# for each outcome and weights matrix

#specify the variable you want to look at
#options: prison_exp_h1, prison_exp_h5, prison_exp_h10, prison_exp_h25, num_prisons_in_puma, prison_present_in_puma

main_x <- "prison_exp_h1"

main_table <- bind_rows(
  # OLS M3 doesn't use the weights, so the same row is repeated for both weights matrices
  ols_m3 %>%
    filter(x == main_x) %>%
    expand_grid(w = names(weight_labels)) %>%
    transmute(y, w, model = "OLS M3 (state-clustered SEs)", effect = "Coefficient",
              estimate = ols_estimate, std.error = ols_se, p.value = ols_p,
              spatial_param = NA_real_, aic = NA_real_),

  # SEM: exposure coefficient, with lambda and AIC
  error_results %>%
    filter(x == main_x) %>%
    select(y, w, sem_coef, sem_lambda, sem_aic) %>%
    unnest(sem_coef) %>%
    transmute(y, w, model = "SEM", effect = "Coefficient",
              estimate, std.error, p.value,
              spatial_param = sem_lambda, aic = sem_aic),

  # SDEM direct: exposure in the PUMA itself (lambda and AIC shown on this row)
  error_results %>%
    filter(x == main_x) %>%
    select(y, w, sdem_direct, sdem_lambda, sdem_aic) %>%
    unnest(sdem_direct) %>%
    transmute(y, w, model = "SDEM", effect = "Direct",
              estimate, std.error, p.value,
              spatial_param = sdem_lambda, aic = sdem_aic),

  # SDEM indirect: exposure in neighboring PUMAs
  error_results %>%
    filter(x == main_x) %>%
    select(y, w, sdem_indirect) %>%
    unnest(sdem_indirect) %>%
    transmute(y, w, model = "SDEM", effect = "Indirect (neighbors)",
              estimate, std.error, p.value,
              spatial_param = NA_real_, aic = NA_real_),

  # SDEM total: direct + indirect
  error_results %>%
    filter(x == main_x) %>%
    select(y, w, sdem_total) %>%
    unnest(sdem_total) %>%
    transmute(y, w, model = "SDEM", effect = "Total",
              estimate, std.error, p.value,
              spatial_param = NA_real_, aic = NA_real_)
) %>%
  mutate(outcome = outcomes[y],
         weights = weight_labels[w],
         model   = factor(model, levels = c("OLS M3 (state-clustered SEs)", "SEM", "SDEM")),
         effect  = factor(effect, levels = c("Coefficient", "Direct",
                                             "Indirect (neighbors)", "Total"))) %>%
  arrange(outcome, weights, model, effect)

main_table %>%
  select(outcome, weights, model, effect, estimate, std.error, p.value, spatial_param, aic) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = c("outcome", "weights")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(estimate, std.error, spatial_param), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = p.value, decimals = 4) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = aic, decimals = 1) %>%
  sub_missing(missing_text = "") %>%
  cols_label(model = "Model", effect = "Effect", estimate = "β", std.error = "SE",
             p.value = "p", spatial_param = "λ", aic = "AIC") %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"), locations = cells_body(rows = p.value < 0.05)) %>%
  tab_header(title = paste0("Main exposure (", exposures[[main_x]], ", per SD): OLS vs. spatial error models"),
             subtitle = "λ = spatial error parameter (how strongly neighboring PUMAs share unexplained variation). Shaded: p < 0.05")
```

## All exposure measures: OLS vs. SEM vs. SDEM

```{r}
#| label: p6-all-table
error_results %>%
  mutate(sem = sem_coef, direct = sdem_direct, indirect = sdem_indirect) %>%
  select(y, x, w, sem, direct, indirect, sem_lambda) %>%
  unnest_wider(sem,      names_sep = "_") %>%
  unnest_wider(direct,   names_sep = "_") %>%
  unnest_wider(indirect, names_sep = "_") %>%
  left_join(ols_m3, by = c("y", "x")) %>%
  mutate(outcome  = outcomes[y],
         exposure = factor(exposures[x], levels = exposures),
         weights  = weight_labels[w]) %>%
  arrange(outcome, weights, exposure) %>%
  select(outcome, weights, exposure,
         ols_estimate, ols_p,
         sem_estimate, sem_p.value,
         direct_estimate, direct_p.value,
         indirect_estimate, indirect_p.value,
         sem_lambda) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = c("outcome", "weights")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(ols_estimate, sem_estimate, direct_estimate, indirect_estimate, sem_lambda),
             decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(ols_p, sem_p.value, direct_p.value, indirect_p.value), decimals = 4) %>%
  cols_label(exposure = "Exposure", ols_estimate = "OLS β", ols_p = "p",
             sem_estimate = "SEM β", sem_p.value = "p",
             direct_estimate = "SDEM direct", direct_p.value = "p",
             indirect_estimate = "SDEM indirect", indirect_p.value = "p",
             sem_lambda = "SEM λ") %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "OLS M3", columns = c(ols_estimate, ols_p)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "SEM", columns = c(sem_estimate, sem_p.value, sem_lambda)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "SDEM", columns = c(direct_estimate, direct_p.value,
                                          indirect_estimate, indirect_p.value)) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Exposure coefficients: OLS M3 vs. spatial error models",
             subtitle = "Continuous exposures per SD; presence = with vs. without")
```

## Model checks

Three checks for the exposure chosen in `main_x`: a Hausman test (do OLS and SEM coefficients differ more than chance allows?), Moran's I on the SEM and SDEM residuals (should be close to zero), and AIC for OLS M3, SEM and SDEM (lower is better).

```{r}
#| label: p6-checks
# Hausman test: do OLS and SEM coefficients differ more than chance allows?
hausman_safe <- possibly(Hausman.test, otherwise = list(statistic = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_))

hausman <- error_models %>%
  filter(x == main_x) %>%
  mutate(test      = map(sem, hausman_safe),
         statistic = map_dbl(test, ~ unname(.x$statistic)),
         p.value   = map_dbl(test, ~ .x$p.value)) %>%
  transmute(outcome = outcomes[y], weights = weight_labels[w], statistic, p.value)
hausman

# Is spatial structure left in the residuals of SEM and SDEM? (should be close to zero)
resid_moran <- error_models %>%
  filter(x == main_x) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(sem, sdem), names_to = "model", values_to = "fit") %>%
  mutate(
    lw = map2(y, w, ~ p6_weights[[.x]][[.y]]),
    e  = map(fit, ~ as.vector(.x$y - .x$X %*% .x$coefficients)),
    u  = pmap(list(e, fit, lw), ~ ..1 - ..2$lambda * lag.listw(..3, ..1, zero.policy = TRUE)),
    moran_I = map2_dbl(u, lw, ~ unname(moran.test(.x, .y, zero.policy = TRUE)$estimate[1])),
    moran_p = map2_dbl(u, lw, ~ moran.test(.x, .y, zero.policy = TRUE)$p.value)
  ) %>%
  transmute(outcome = outcomes[y], weights = weight_labels[w],
            model = toupper(model), moran_I, moran_p)
resid_moran

# Fit across models for the main measure (lower AIC = better).

error_results %>%
  filter(x == main_x) %>%
  select(y, w, sem_aic, sdem_aic) %>%
  left_join(p5_models %>%
              filter(x == main_x) %>%
              transmute(y, ols_aic = map_dbl(model, AIC)),
            by = "y") %>%
  mutate(outcome = outcomes[y], weights = weight_labels[w]) %>%
  select(outcome, weights, `OLS M3` = ols_aic, SEM = sem_aic, SDEM = sdem_aic)
```

# OVERDOSE GEOGRAPHY

```{r}
#| label: cdc-split
# tract x year overdose file (from the processing notebook)
# group_id = CDC unit, GEOID = tract, GEOID20 = PUMA, tot_pop = 2020 population
tract_od <- read_csv("data/final/tract_overdose_by_year_2022_2024.csv",
                     col_types = cols(GEOID = col_character(), GEOID20 = col_character(),
                                      group_id = col_character()))

# for every CDC unit and year: how many tracts and how many PUMAs it covers
cdc_groups <- tract_od %>%
  group_by(group_id, year) %>%
  summarise(n_tracts = n(),
            n_pumas  = n_distinct(GEOID20, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups  = "drop") %>%
  mutate(split = n_pumas > 1)

# how many units are split (a one-tract unit can't be split, so I also show multi-tract units)
cdc_groups %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(units          = n(),
            multi_tract    = sum(n_tracts > 1),
            split          = sum(split),
            share_of_multi = split / multi_tract)

# for every PUMA: share of its population (and deaths) coming from split units
puma_split <- tract_od %>%
  filter(!is.na(GEOID20)) %>%
  left_join(cdc_groups %>% select(group_id, year, split), by = c("group_id", "year")) %>%
  group_by(GEOID20) %>%
  summarise(share_split_pop    = weighted.mean(split, tot_pop, na.rm = TRUE),
            share_split_deaths = weighted.mean(split, deaths, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(split_level = cut(share_split_pop, breaks = c(-Inf, 0, 0.25, 0.5, Inf),
                           labels = c("None", "Low", "Moderate", "High")))

# how many PUMAs are in each level
puma_split %>%
  count(split_level) %>%
  mutate(share = n / sum(n))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-cdc-split-map
#| fig-height: 6
puma_geo_l48 %>%
  select(GEOID20) %>%
  left_join(puma_split, by = "GEOID20") %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = split_level), colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(None = "grey92", Low = "#C6DBEF", Moderate = "#6BAED6",
                               High = "#08519C"),
                    labels = c("None", "Low (≤ 25%)", "Moderate (25–50%)", "High (> 50%)"),
                    na.value = "white",
                    name = "Share of PUMA population\nfrom split CDC units") +
  labs(title = "Overdose rates built from CDC units shared with another PUMA") +
  theme_void()
```

## Is the clustering still there where the outcome is built cleanly?

All on the M3 residuals for overdose (h = 10 km):

1. Local Moran's I by split level: is clustering stronger in PUMAs
   built from shared units?
2. Moran's I only among None/Low PUMAs vs. only among Moderate/High.
3. M3 without the High PUMAs: do the coefficient and the clustering
   change?

```{r}
#| label: cdc-moran
y_od <- "overdose_rate_2022_2024"
f_od <- as.formula(str_c(y_od, " ~ prison_exp_h10 + ", ctrl_str[y_od], " + factor(state_fips)"))

# overdose sample with boundaries (projected, so snap = 1 means 1 m) and split levels
geo_od <- puma_geo %>%
  st_transform(5070) %>%
  select(GEOID20) %>%
  inner_join(model_data[[y_od]], by = "GEOID20") %>%
  left_join(puma_split %>% select(GEOID20, share_split_pop, split_level), by = "GEOID20")

m_od  <- lm(f_od, data = st_drop_geometry(geo_od))
lw_od <- nb2listw(poly2nb(geo_od, queen = TRUE, snap = 1), style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)

# 1. local Moran's I of the residuals for every PUMA, averaged by split level
local_moran_split <- geo_od %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  mutate(local_I = localmoran(residuals(m_od), lw_od, zero.policy = TRUE)[, "Ii"]) %>%
  select(GEOID20, split_level, share_split_pop, local_I)

local_moran_split %>%
  group_by(split_level) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_local_I = mean(local_I), share_positive = mean(local_I > 0)) %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(mean_local_I, share_positive), decimals = 3) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Residual clustering by share of PUMA from split CDC units")

# same question without categories: does clustering rise with the split share?
cor.test(local_moran_split$local_I, local_moran_split$share_split_pop, method = "spearman")

# 2. and 3. Moran's I in subsets, and M3 without the High PUMAs
subsets <- list(`All PUMAs`        = geo_od,
                `None or Low`      = geo_od %>% filter(split_level %in% c("None", "Low")),
                `Moderate or High` = geo_od %>% filter(split_level %in% c("Moderate", "High")),
                `Without High`     = geo_od %>% filter(split_level != "High"))

imap_dfr(subsets, ~ {
  m  <- lm(f_od, data = st_drop_geometry(.x))
  lw <- nb2listw(poly2nb(.x, queen = TRUE, snap = 1), style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)
  tibble(sample        = .y,
         n             = nobs(m),
         prison_coef   = coef(m)[["prison_exp_h10"]],
         resid_moran_I = lm.morantest(m, lw, zero.policy = TRUE)$estimate[[1]])
}) %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(prison_coef, resid_moran_I), decimals = 3) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Residual Moran's I and prison coefficient by subset (M3, h = 10 km)")
```
